legal.draftNotice: Draft. Written to cover what Google asks for to verify the app; worth having a lawyer read it before charging anyone.
legal.privacyIntro: Morchitask is a daily planning app. This explains what it stores, why, and how to get it out or delete it.
legal.pS1Body: Your name, email and profile picture, which come from your Google account when you sign in. The content you create: tasks, notes, categories, goals, routines, schedules and tracked time. And your preferences: language, theme, daily capacity and reminders.
legal.pS2Title: What we do with your Google Calendar
legal.pS2Body: If you connect your calendar we ask for two permissions. «See events» shows your events for the day inside the Day view, so you can plan around them. «Manage events» creates, updates and deletes only the events matching time blocks you scheduled in the app. We don't read or touch anything else in your calendar, and we don't use that data for advertising or sell it.
legal.pS3Body: The database is on Neon and the app runs on Vercel. Files you attach are stored in Vercel Blob. Your Google token stays on the server and is never sent to the browser.
legal.pS4Body: Nobody, other than the providers above, who process it so the app works. If you invite someone into your space, they see only the tasks you marked as shared.
legal.pS5Body: From Settings you can export everything as a file, and delete your account. Deleting is permanent and immediate: tasks, notes, files and profile all go. We keep no copy.
legal.pS6Body: If this changes in a way that matters, we'll email you before it takes effect.
legal.termsIntro: The rules for using Morchitask. In plain language, and they're the ones that apply.
legal.tS1Body: A personal daily planning app, for one person, with the option to share tasks with one other. It isn't a team tool and it doesn't promise uninterrupted availability.
legal.tS2Body: You sign in with Google. You're responsible for what happens with your account and for the content you upload. One account is one person.
legal.tS3Body: The trial lasts {days} days and asks for no card. When it ends, access stops: nothing is charged automatically. If you subscribe, the price is ${price} per month or ${yearly} per year, and you can cancel any time from Settings, keeping access until the paid period ends.
legal.tS4Body: If something went wrong, write to us within 30 days and we'll refund it. We'd rather do that than have you stuck with something you don't use.
legal.tS5Body: Don't use the app for anything illegal, don't try to break it, don't resell access. We can close an account that does.
legal.tS6Body: The service is provided as is. We take backups and we're careful, but we're not liable for indirect losses. Export your data if it's critical.
legal.tS7Body: You can leave any time by deleting your account. If we ever had to shut the service down, we'd give at least 30 days' notice and you could export everything.
legal.tS8Body: Governed by the laws of the Argentine Republic.
legal.pAnalyticsBody: On the public pages we use Vercel Web Analytics to know how many people visit and where they come from. It sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser: a visit is identified by a code built from the connection and discarded after 24 hours, so nobody can be followed from one day to the next or across sites. Before each visit is sent we strip everything after «?» or «#» from the address. We don't use it for advertising or link it to your account.

help.title: Help
help.lead: Just enough to get going, and how to reach us if something's off.
help.morningBody: You bring in what's left from yesterday and estimate how long each thing takes. The bar tells you whether it fits in your hours.
help.dayBody: Drag it to a time and it stays. If the day falls apart, Replan moves what's left from now on.
help.nightBody: You see what you did and how long it took, and decide where each loose end goes. Then you switch off.
help.shortcutsNote: {os, select, mac {We detected a Mac from your browser. Single-letter shortcuts don't work while you're typing.} other {We detected Windows or Linux from your browser. Single-letter shortcuts don't work while you're typing.}}
help.faqTrialQ: What happens when the trial ends?
help.faqTrialA: Access stops, and the app warns you in the last few days. Nothing is charged automatically: we never asked for your card. Your data stays, and you can download it or delete the account.
help.faqTwoQ: How much is it for two of us?
help.faqTwoA: The same. One plan covers your space: you and one more person. Whoever pays for it manages it.
help.faqWhoA: Polar, which sells Morchitask for us and handles taxes and invoices. That's why the receipt comes from Polar.
help.faqCardA: Polar retries for about 14 days, and meanwhile you keep using the app. Whoever manages the plan updates the card from Plan and billing.
help.faqCancelA: Yes, whoever manages the plan cancels it from Plan and billing. You keep access until the end of the period you paid for.
help.faqDataQ: What happens to my data if I leave?
help.faqDataA: You can export it whenever you want and delete the account from Settings. Deleting is final: everything of yours goes and no copy is kept. If you share the space, the shared tasks stay with the other person.
help.contactBody: A person reads it, not a bot. Tell us what you were doing and what you expected to happen.
